corrections.subject: NavigatorMoveToRange 008a2f20
corrections.was: the packet brief expected a target plus a range argument
corrections.is: the binding reads Lua arguments 0 and 1 only and has no range argument
corrections.evidence: 008A2FFD pushes index 0 and 008A3036 pushes index 1 into 00B677E0; there is no third BSP_LuaObject_ArgumentAt in the body 008A2F20-008A30C2, and 0077D600's three stack arguments at 008A3069/008A306F/008A3070 are flags 1, the descriptor and the command object.

corrections.subject: the moveto family
corrections.was: NavigatorMoveToPos, NavigatorDirectMoveToRange and NavigatorMoveToRange read as three behaviours
corrections.is: three Lua names for one native routine
corrections.evidence: 008a2bc0, 008a2d70 and 008a2f20 have identical bodies of 0x1a2 bytes and all three PUSH 0xe08f68 (008A2D10, 008A2EC0, 008A3070); they differ only in the dead error-prefix length (0x20, 0x28, 0x22) and the one-time luakod guard global.

corrections.subject: Ghidra's unreachable-block warnings
corrections.was: the decompiler reports 'Removing unreachable block' at 008a3110 and 008a316c (and the matching pairs in 008a2f20, 008a2bc0, 008a2d70, 00899d10)
corrections.is: those blocks are reachable; they build and immediately free the 'luaMW_<name> failed:' prefix string
corrections.evidence: 008A30FB/008A30FF zero the string object before 0041DD40 writes through ECX; Ghidra's prototype does not model that write, so it folds CMP EDI,EBP at 008A310C to always-equal. 008AD330 uses the same idiom with a different stack layout and decompiles with the memcpy visible, and its length 0x1A equals strlen("luaMW_RepairEnable failed:").

corrections.subject: JoinFormation direction
corrections.was: unknown which of the two entities becomes leader
corrections.is: Lua argument 0 is the follower, Lua argument 1 the leader
corrections.evidence: 00899E59 puts argument 0 in ECX and 00899E58 pushes argument 1; 0077C8F8 then asks ECX's vtable[16Ch] whether it may 'follow' the stack argument, and 0077C92B takes the message's +20h id from the stack argument.

corrections.subject: vtable slot 16Ch
corrections.was: read from the call site as 'apply the follow command'
corrections.is: a bool-returning availability predicate; 0077C8D0 issues no command
corrections.evidence: MDestroyer's vtable base is 00CFC3D0 because [00CFC3D0+160h] is 00816E30; [00CFC3D0+16Ch] is 008162B0, whose body 008162B0-00816408 returns bool and dispatches only IsKindOf tests and BSP_CString_CompareInsensitive. A false answer makes 0077C8D0 return with no effect at 0077C902.

run.luaInit: ok (default run without --stand-in-random still fails at Scripts/global/commandhelpers.lua:1003, reproducing docs/GAME_EXECUTABLE.md milestone 2l)
run.stand_in_random: the native row `random` 0088C160 is NOT reconstructed by this packet and is not in its lease; --stand-in-random is a deterministic probe fixture with the native's argument-count shape and none of its numerics, present only so luaInit runs past luaPickRnd. Every ship row below depends on it.
run.note_on_counts: These are larger than docs/GAME_EXECUTABLE.md milestone 2l's (15/14/12/6/1/4) because that run resolves FindEntity only over the 32 created scene instances, while this probe mints an entity for every entity-returning row, so more of the script's branches run. JoinFormation and NavigatorMoveToRange and SetRoleAvailable match exactly.
run.attackmove_targets_depend_on_random: the six Haguro..Harusame rows and the eight Yamakaze..Hatsukaze rows pick their target through luaPickRnd, so the target column is a function of the --stand-in-random fixture, not of the native. The ship column is not: those loops are over fixed FindEntity lists.
run.self_follow_rows: DeRuyter, Houston and Exeter follow themselves because usn_2_java's loops run over the whole group including index 1 and call JoinFormation(unit, group[1]) for every member (Scripts/missions/usn/usn_2_java.lua:210-228). Whether the native accepts a self-follow is decided by the unread predicate 008162B0; the probe answers it true for every call.
